name: Eusebio Ochoa
description: '''Eusebio Ochoa Isaza''' (2 October 1880 – 24 September 1955) was a Colombian musician and composer of [[pasillo]]s and [[bambuco]]s. In July 1910 he recorded in New York with the ensemble La Lira Antioqueña for the [[Columbia Phonograph Company]]; the sessions included a version of the [[National Anthem of Colombia|Colombian national anthem]] often described in Colombia as the anthem's first phonographic recording. His best-known composition is the bambuco "El profesor de canto". He later taught at the Institute of Fine Arts of Medellín, where he became dean of the teaching staff.
